primitive.migration_notes: C2 (2026-10-02, lancelot): the three exact-one-incidence copies now unfold to GTBase.common.perfect_matching M (= matching M /\ cover M = [set: G]); the names stay as transparent aliases for one migration cycle. X18's and X25's frozen chains were already built by C1 (Packing.migration.matching.X18Legacy) and M1 (Packing.migration.simple_edges.X25Legacy): their frozen bodies and theorem statements are preserved, only x18_perfect_matching_compat and x25_perfect_matching_compat are re-proved through perfect_matching_exactly_oneP, and the per-area entry point Packing.migration.perfect_matching states this family's helper and row certificates over those frozen bodies. X24's chain and pre-M1 edge set are frozen in Cycle.migration.perfect_matching. Edge partitions and edge families are the next family.

exactly-one-incidence.note: members are edges (X18 through C1's matching alias) and every vertex lies in exactly one member; equivalent to matching plus cover without any guard

upstream_audit.note: coq-graph-theory 0.9.7 defines connectivity.matching but no perfect-matching predicate; GTBase.common.perfect_matching (matching M /\ cover M = [set: G], with perfect_matching_K2 and not_perfect_matching0 since WP4b) is the canonical. The corpus copies spell it as exact-one incidence of every vertex; perfect_matching_exactly_oneP proves the two readings equivalent (members are 2-sets, so cover and exactly-one agree), card_perfect_matching gives #|G| = 2 * #|M| and the odd-order and K_3 negatives.
